clue.text: Guard's demand may be too much to swallow

definitions.meaning: the payment a railway guard asks of a passenger travelling beyond the ticket's limit
read literally, a surplus of food, more than one can eat

explanation.surface: A railway guard asks for something so outrageous that the passenger cannot accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too much to swallow' usually means unbelievable; here it is read literally as an excess of food (fare). A British train guard collects the extra charge from someone who has gone past their ticket's limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge levied on board a train, and also, read as two words, a surplus of food.

clue.text: Prophet, last of sequence in period

indicators.note: the letter for the end of the sequence goes inside the word for a period

parts.note: an era is a period of history
Z is the last letter of the alphabet, the best-known sequence of letters

explanation.surface: A list of prophets ends with the latest of them, placed within a particular age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of sequence' tempts you to take the final letter of the word 'sequence' (E); it means the end of the alphabet's sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is an Old Testament figure, a scribe and priest counted among the Hebrew prophets.

clue.text: Final section programmer announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so the word for a programmer is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a coder writes computer programs

explanation.surface: A software developer declares the last part of the project.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CODER and CODA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a coda is the concluding passage of a piece or movement.

clue.text: Horror — cup of tea isn't stirred

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dismay at finding a cup of tea that has not been stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' rearranges the twelve letters of CUP OF TEA ISNT; 'stirred' looks like part of the tea-making picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupefaction is stunned amazement, the dumbfounded state that shock or dismay produces.

clue.text: Give up game after hearing warning

indicators.note: the word for a game comes after the sound of the warning
on hearing the warning word, we take its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning to people in the ball's path
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the match after being told to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE, the golfer's cry, sounds like FOR; GO is the oriental board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it, to relinquish it voluntarily.

clue.text: Country for hunter and angler, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Open terrain suits both the hunter and the fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AND ANGLER; 'angler' seems to be a second sportsman alongside the hunter, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangeland is open grassland or scrub where animals roam and graze, and so where game is pursued.

clue.text: Stick book in the post

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a volume through the letterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the post' looks like the mail; it is a doorpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the upright side piece of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Man of principle half rises in ecclesiastical court

indicators.note: the reversed word for half sits inside the name of the church court

parts.note: the Court of Arches is the Church of England's appeal court for the province of Canterbury

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word half is read from bottom to top

parts.note: demi means half, as in demigod

explanation.surface: A principled man climbs halfway up within a church tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns DEMI upwards into IMED, placed in ARCHES. 'Man of principle' sounds like a moral person; it is the mathematician behind Archimedes' principle of buoyancy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek scientist gave his name to the principle that a body immersed in fluid loses weight equal to the fluid displaced.

clue.text: Bird seeing gun goes to ground

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird spots a firearm and dives for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges GOES TO into TGOOSE; 'goes to ground' reads as hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent goose is a small dark goose that winters on northern European coasts.

clue.text: Bloody dog! — tirade is something fruity

parts.note: something bloody is red with blood
a cur is a mongrel dog
a rant is a long angry outburst

explanation.surface: Someone curses a dog and launches into a fruity tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British swear word in the surface; it supplies the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A redcurrant is a small red berry grown on garden bushes.

clue.text: Extent of crusaders' objective?

definitions.meaning: a measure of land area, 4840 square yards
the port city in the Holy Land that crusading armies besieged and captured

explanation.surface: How far the crusaders' goals extended.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measurement, and Acre is the city in modern Israel taken in the Third Crusade.

clue.text: Endless speed is opening setter up for reprimand

indicators.note: the speed and is pieces open up the setter word and sit inside it

parts.note: cement is something that sets hard

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off the word for speed

parts.note: haste is speed

explanation.surface: A rushed attempt to open the crossword compiler's mind ends in a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler; here it is a substance that sets hard. 'Endless' trims the speed word, and 'opening' (with 'up', as in opening up) splits the setter to take in the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastisement is a severe rebuke or punishment.

clue.text: In the old days, British Columbia shrank, then expanded

parts.note: the Canadian province's name shortened to its two initials, which then open out into a different phrase with the same abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Canadian province shrinks and then grows again.
explanation.walkthrough: British Columbia abbreviates to BC; BC is also the dating abbreviation for years before the Christian era, which spelt out gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates in the era preceding the birth of Jesus are ancient, long ago.

clue.text: Keep talking to new, marvellous boy

parts.note: to chatter is to talk on and on
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges a remarkable young newcomer to carry on talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth called the poet Thomas Chatterton, who died at seventeen, 'the marvellous boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Wordsworth's tribute to the teenage poet and forger of medieval verse.

clue.text: Use services of wernham Hogg, where business is down

definitions.meaning: Wernham Hogg is the paper merchant in the British TV comedy The Office, so you would buy stationery from them
the daily agenda listing the business to be taken in Parliament

explanation.surface: Dealing with the firm from The Office, where trade is slow.
explanation.walkthrough: Wernham Hogg is the fictional Slough paper company in the British sitcom The Office. 'business is down' sounds like falling trade; it means business written down on the agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a request for stationery, and the printed parliamentary schedule of the day's proceedings.

clue.text: Woman graduate about to change short drink

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: the graduate's letters go round the shortened word for change

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the verb

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A female graduate is about to swap to a small measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short drink' looks like a measure of spirits, but 'short' trims the verb and only 'drink' defines. 'about' wraps the graduate's letters round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs in hot water, such as camomile or mint, is drunk like tea.

clue.text: Dump arctic explorer across river — it's a long way away?

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

indicators.note: the explorer's name stretches across the letter for river

parts.note: Robert Peary was the American who claimed to reach the North Pole

explanation.surface: A rubbish heap and an explorer straddling a river, somewhere far off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the First World War song 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary'; Tipperary is an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: The marching song says this Irish town is a long way away, so the place is defined by its lyric.

clue.text: Water flowing back round handle

indicators.note: a river flowing back is read from right to left

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A stream curls back around a door handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing back' turns TEES into SEET. 'Water' looks like the definition or something to drink; it is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to a task is to deal with it, attend to it.

clue.text: Robin's short message?

parts.note: a small bird's chirp, and also a brief post on a social media site whose emblem is a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A bird's chirping call shares its name with a brief online post.

clue.text: Designs up for review, needing slimming down in this state

definitions.text: needing slimming down in this state

indicators.note: something put up for review is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion sketches submitted for assessment, with a note that some models need to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges DESIGNS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpness is the condition in which someone would need to lose weight.

clue.text: Detailed plan is concept that has been refuted

definitions.meaning: a technical drawing showing the parts of a machine separated but in their relative positions
an idea that has been discredited, as a theory is said to be blown apart

explanation.surface: A thorough design turns out to rest on a disproved idea.
explanation.walkthrough: A theory is said to be exploded when it is disproved, and a view is an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineering diagram with components drawn apart, and an opinion that has been discredited.

clue.text: Star name, one not using animals

parts.note: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity's name, a person who avoids animal products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is an actual star.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats no meat, dairy or other animal products.

clue.text: To lose weight, steals fruit

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken out of the word for steals

parts.note: whips is slang for steals

explanation.surface: Someone shoplifts fruit while on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' is British slang for steal; 'lose weight' looks like dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hips are the red berries left on a rose bush after flowering.

clue.text: Go with purpose

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Set off with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with purpose' looks like a single adverb describing the going.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend one's way is to travel or proceed, often slowly.

clue.text: Leading individual that goes ahead

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
I is a single person, oneself

explanation.surface: The front runner is the one who forges on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes ahead' reads as 'goes a head': a topi is a pith helmet worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet, something placed on the head.

clue.text: Flower child welcomes controversialist

indicators.note: the child word takes in the other word, which sits inside it

parts.note: a mite is a small child
an arguer is someone who argues

explanation.surface: A flower child greets a combative speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower child' looks like a hippy; the phrase splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marguerite is the ox-eye daisy, a white-petalled garden flower.

clue.text: Fate of anti-navy slogan?

parts.note: an anti slogan says no to something
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The destiny of a protest chant against the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: A placard reading NO RN would be an anti-navy slogan. In Norse myth the Norns are the three Fates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norns are the Norse goddesses of destiny, like the Fates of Greek myth.

clue.text: The pony is sick — died, put to sleep

indicators.note: sick suggests something in a bad way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet reports that an ailing pony has died after being put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges THE PONY IS; 'put to sleep' looks like putting the animal down, but it means sent into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotised means placed in a trance, a sleeplike state.
